You don't need long context
Peter Belcak, Saurav Muralidharan, Jindong Jiang

Abstract. Later tokens are costlier to generate than earlier tokens.

1 Introduction
Not all tokens are generated equal. Token generation latency and memory
footprint both grow with the number of tokens in a language model's context.

Figure 1: The cost of long context. Dollar cost of generating 1M output
tokens on an existing input KV cache as a function of the context window
size.

2 Methodology
We use several context-management regimes throughout this work.

3.2 Method
We describe the compaction method used throughout this section, including
the end-of-conversation compaction (EoCC) procedure and how it differs from
full-history accumulation (FHA).

Table 2: Compute per trial
GPU-hours spent per evaluation trial across the
long-horizon benchmark suite.

6 Conclusion
Our experiments show that long contexts are not strictly necessary for
either long-horizon or long-input tasks when frequent compaction is used.

A What characterizes a good compaction?
It is a common experience of human-in-the-loop agent-aided SWE workflows
that after a compaction is performed, certain crucial information disappears.
